results.title: Top court overturns 15-year prison term for ex-PM Han over martial law role
results.content: The Supreme Court on Thursday overturned a 15-year prison sentence for former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo over his role in former President Yoon Suk Yeol's failed martial law bid, sending the case back to an appeals court for review. The top court remanded the case to the Seoul High Court after partially finding issues with the lower ruling. The appellate court sentenced Han to the prison term on multiple charges, including playing a key role in an insurrection in connection with Yoon's emergency decree. The Supreme Court ruling comes about 14 months after special counsel Cho Eun-suk's team indicted the former prime minister in August last year.

results.title: IAEA issues first report on Korea's nuclear-powered sub project
results.content: The U.N. nuclear watchdog on Thursday released its first report on Korea's project to build nuclear-powered submarines, expressing satisfaction over related cooperation with the Asian country, according to Seoul's foreign ministry. The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) issued the report, titled "Naval Nuclear Propulsion: Republic of Korea," under the name of Director General Rafael Grossi as it discussed the report during its Board of Governors' meeting in Vienna this week. The report came as Korea and the IAEA have begun consultations on safeguards and other matters related to the submarine project. The IAEA has been issuing annual reports on Australia and Brazil since 2022 and 2023, respectively, as the two countries have been in consultation with the agency over their submarine projects. results.title: 'Phantom of the Opera' composer eager to explore Korea's homegrown musicals
results.content: British composer Andrew Lloyd Webber behind globally recognized musicals including "Phantom of the Opera" said Thursday that he is eager to explore Korea’s homegrown musicals during his stay and promised to return next year to watch more. He is in Seoul this week to promote "Phantom of the Opera," which celebrates 40th anniversary of its premiere — it premiered in Korea 25 years ago. The British composer acknowledged that the trip was overdue. “I’ve been feeling a little bit ashamed of myself for not having come here earlier,” he said. “But this time I thought, I’ve got to come to Korea. I really must see what’s going on.” About the active musical scene in Korea with many local productions making their own works, he said: “I think it’s fantastic to know that there is a musical theater culture coming from actually the country itself. results.title: CSAT exam writers to be released after 40 days of isolation for security
results.content: Exam writers and reviewers for this year's national college entrance exam were set to be released Thursday, after spending some 40 days to produce error-free questions in isolation, continuing the long tradition of the practice repeated each year to preserve the integrity of the high-stakes exam. According to the Korea Institute for Curriculum and Evaluation (KICE), around 500 test writers and reviewers, along with about 280 administrative staff, began their seclusion at an undisclosed facility in early- to mid-October to craft Thursday's College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT). They were set to be released after the exam concludes at 5:45 p.m. Known locally as the Suneung, the CSAT is a pivotal milestone in Korea that heavily influences students' university admissions, future career paths and social standing. Such importance of the exam to many, if not all, students puts immense pressure

results.title: Korea's largest game show G-STAR at crossroads as top studios look abroad
results.content: Launched in 2005, G-STAR has been widely considered a barometer of South Korea's gaming industry, giving developers a stage to debut upcoming titles, and facilitating cross-border exchanges between local studios and overseas publishers. Despite ups and downs, including a complete cancellation during the COVID-19 pandemic, the annual event has maintained its reputation as South Korea's flagship game fair. After two decades, however, the event is now at a crossroads. Despite efforts to expand its scope into other sectors, such as webtoons and motor racing, major domestic game companies are turning away from the event and visitor numbers are declining. Three of the country's biggest game companies -- NC Corp., Netmarble Corp. and Nexon Games Co. -- were absent from this year's G-STAR, which kicked off its three-day run in the southeastern port city of Busan on Thursday. results.title: Lotte Hotels & Resorts hosts kimchi-making event for foreign ambassadors
results.content: Lotte Hotels & Resorts hosted its annual kimchi-making event for foreign ambassadors in Korea at its Signiel Seoul hotel on Monday, introducing the diplomats to Korea's traditional food culture and spirit of sharing ahead of Kimchi Day on Sunday, the hotel operator said Thursday. Now in its second year, the event brought together 35 ambassadors to Korea to experience "kimjang," Korea's traditional winter kimchi-making and sharing practice, which was recognized by UNESCO as an intangible cultural heritage in 2013. Lotte said the program showed Korea's spirit of sharing, with neighbors coming together to prepare food for winter. After making the kimchi, participants received a portion of their freshly made batch packed in "onggi," traditional Korean earthenware jars, so they could enjoy it at home. results.title: Silent DJ party draws 2,000 dancers to Seoul's Mount Nam
results.content: Seoul’s autumn nights took on a club-like atmosphere Sunday as about 2,000 people gathered at Mount Nam in the center of the capital for a silent DJ party — where dancers tune into live sets through wireless headphones rather than loudspeakers — turning one of the city’s best-known scenic spots into an open-air dance floor. The event, dubbed Palgak Club, closed out the inaugural 2026 Namsan Night Festival, an initiative by the Seoul Metropolitan Government to expand nighttime leisure options and draw more visitors to surrounding neighborhoods. At Mount Nam Palgakjeong Plaza on Sunday, the headphone-driven format let crowds dance to live DJs without blasting music over conventional speakers, cutting down on noise complaints around the hillside landmark. The event ran in two sessions, from 5:30 p.m. to 7 p.m. and from 7:30 p.m. to 9 p.m., with music spanning several genres and participants

results.title: 2 men sentenced to prison terms over killing of film director
results.content: Two men indicted on charges of assaulting and killing indie film director Kim Chang-min last year were sentenced Thursday to prison terms of 12 years and three years, respectively. The Namyangju branch of the Uijeongbu District Court handed down a 12-year term to a 32-year-old man surnamed Lee and a three-year term to another 32-year-old surnamed Lim. The court also banned the two men from working at institutions serving people with disabilities for five to 10 years. Lee and Lim were accused of beating Kim severely with their fists and feet at a restaurant in Guri, just east of Seoul, on Oct. 20, 2025, following a dispute over noise. Kim was taken to a hospital, where he was declared brain-dead 17 days later. He subsequently died after donating his organs to four recipients. The defendants were also charged with violating the Act on Welfare of Persons with Disabilities by assaulting Kim

results.title: Lawmaker reassures Iran envoy that Cheonghae Unit expansion is not war move
results.content: The chair of the National Assembly’s Foreign Affairs and Unification Committee told Iran’s newly appointed ambassador to Korea that the planned expansion of the Cheonghae Unit’s operational area near the Strait of Hormuz is aimed solely at ensuring freedom of navigation, not at joining a military campaign against Tehran. “The ambassador expressed concern about military deployment in the strait and I made our position clear that this is not the case,” Rep. Song Seog-jun told The Korea Times Wednesday. Ahmad Erfanian, Iran’s newly appointed ambassador to Korea, paid a courtesy call to Song's office, Monday, and the two exchanged introductory greetings following the ambassador’s appointment and discussed key issues between Korea and Iran. Song said he sought to ease the ambassador’s concerns. “I told him that this is not an expansion of military deployment. Korea is expanding our role only

results.title: Bill to officially recognize more victims of pro-democracy movements introduced at plenary session
results.content: A bill calling for official recognition and welfare benefits for more victims of pro-democracy movements was brought before a parliamentary plenary session Thursday. The bill, tabled by the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK), was immediately met with a filibuster by the main opposition People Power Party (PPP) during the plenary session. The bill is expected to be put to a vote Friday afternoon after the 24-hour filibuster ends. The Democratic Merit Act calls for providing official recognition and benefits to 635 people who were killed, went missing or suffered injuries during pro-democracy movements, including the 1979 Busan-Masan protests and the June 10 democracy uprising in 1987. It seeks to give recognition to victims of past pro-democracy movements who are not covered by current laws, which honor those involved in the April 19 democratic uprising in 1960 and the 1980 pro-democr

results.title: National Museum of Korea sets annual attendance record
results.content: The National Museum of Korea has drawn a record number of visitors this year, the museum said Thursday. The museum recorded 6,508,000 visitors from Jan. 1 to Nov. 18, surpassing the previous annual record of 6,507,483 set last year, it said. Officials expect this year's attendance to reach 7 million by the end of the year if the current trend continues. Reaching that mark would place the museum second only to the Louvre in Paris in annual visitors, based on 2025 data from the British art magazine The Art Newspaper. Last year, the National Museum of Korea was the third most-visited museum, behind the Louvre, with about 9.04 million visitors, and the Vatican Museums, with about 6.93 million.

results.title: Korean brands eye China comeback, but face tougher local rivals
results.content: Korean entertainment and consumer brands are poised to gain greater access to China under a new trade agreement, but they face tougher local competition than when Beijing first restricted Korean cultural exports nearly a decade ago, market watchers said Thursday. Seoul and Beijing agreed Wednesday to expand their free trade agreement to cover services and investment after more than eight years of talks. The deal could boost bilateral services trade, which has long lagged behind merchandise trade. The entertainment industry stands to be among the biggest beneficiaries. China was the world's second-largest content market in 2024 and was growing faster than the U.S. market, according to the Korea Creative Content Agency. results.title: Upgraded FTA expected to boost Korea-China tourism ties, experts say
results.content: The newly agreed expansion of the Korea-China free trade agreement is expected to give a significant boost to Korea's travel industry by opening direct sales channels in China and encouraging broader bilateral tourism exchanges, industry experts said Thursday. While major Korean package tour operators may not immediately jump into competing directly with Chinese travel agencies, the deal will help add more flights between the two countries and boost both inbound and outbound travel demand, they added. On Wednesday, Korea and China reached a substantial conclusion in their follow-up free trade agreement negotiations on services and investment during a bilateral summit held on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources said. results.title: Mount Seorak offers captivating view of late-autumn foliage
results.content: The brightest flames, they say, burn just before going out. The autumn leaves blanketing the mountains in red seemed to be burning with equal intensity, as if sensing the end of their season. By mid-November, the foliage in Naeseorak, the western side of Daecheongbong Peak, had largely faded and fallen, but Oeseorak was still displaying its final burst of color. Even beneath thick fog that limited visibility, the mountains' beauty was impossible to conceal. Peaks emerged through the mist, overlooking forests ablaze with autumn hues. In late fall, Mount Seorak remains beautiful enough to delight even visitors who arrive a little late for the foliage season. Word of its spectacular scenery has crossed oceans. results.title: Expanding Korea-China cultural exchanges
results.content: A day ahead of the historic trilateral meeting between China, the U.S. and Russia, President Lee Jae Myung lifted a hurdle for Korean cultural content in a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, Wednesday. A decade into an unofficial ban China has not formally acknowledged, the two leaders' agreement is expected to clear a path for Korean cultural products. Lee and Xi met for 34 minutes on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, follow-up second-phase free trade negotiations on services and investment that began in 2018. The agreement includes Beijing granting Seoul the most-favored nation status for its movies and games, allowing Korean travel agencies to advance into China's 23 regions and Korean companies to independently operate their brand shops in China as well. results.title: Embrace AI, but invest in detection for high-stakes exams, global experts say amid cheating fears
results.content: Global higher education experts are urging universities to embrace artificial intelligence (AI) as a catalyst for change rather than a threat, calling for a fundamental rethink of how students are assessed. But for high-stakes exams such as Korea's College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), where traditional testing methods are difficult to replace, they stress the need for greater investment in technology to detect AI-assisted cheating. Korea has been gripped by growing fears of AI-assisted cheating, as concerns over the misuse of smart glasses and other wearable devices spread beyond the CSAT to university admissions, campus exams and professional licensing tests. Kuancheng Huang, a professor at National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University in Taiwan, called for greater investment in technology to detect AI-assisted cheating, particularly in high-stakes exams. results.title: Seoul City Hall observatory extends evening hours, opens Sundays
results.content: Visitors to Korea’s capital now have more time to take in its glittering winter skyline, as city extends evening hours at Seoul City Hall Sky Observatory downtown and opens the panoramic viewing deck on Sundays for the first time this season. The expanded schedule will run from Dec. 11, 2026, through Feb. 9, 2027, coinciding with the Seoul Winter Festa and the operation of the Seoul Plaza ice rink, the Seoul Metropolitan Government said. The observatory, located on the eighth and ninth floors of Seoul City Hall’s main building, will remain open until 9 p.m. Monday through Thursday and Sunday, and until 10 p.m. Friday and Saturday. Special hours will allow visitors to stay until midnight on Christmas Eve and New Year’s Eve, while the observatory will close at 10 p.m. on Christmas Day. results.title: Korean Cultural Center opens new state-owned home in Bangkok
results.content: After more than a decade in rented quarters, the Korean Cultural Center in Thailand has opened a permanent five-story headquarters in Bangkok, expanding its stage to meet growing Thai interest in Korean culture. The center will hold its reopening ceremony Thursday at 5 p.m. (local time), welcoming about 100 officials and representatives from the cultural, artistic, business and media sectors of Korea and Thailand. Located on Sukhumvit Road, one of Bangkok's busiest commercial districts, the 1,906-square-meter building is the 14th Korean cultural center overseas to move into state-owned premises. The center, which opened in 2013, previously faced limitations because its leased facilities lacked a proper performance hall and sufficient classrooms. results.title: Incumbent KBO commissioner elected to 3rd term
results.content: The Korea Baseball Organization (KBO) announced Thursday its incumbent commissioner, Heo Koo-youn, has been unanimously elected for a third term beginning in January 2027. The KBO's board of governors, made up of the 10 club owners, submitted their written votes Wednesday to elect him as its 26th commissioner, more than three weeks after the board of directors, comprising club presidents, had unanimously nominated Heo as commissioner. Heo, 75, became the third commissioner in KBO history to win three consecutive terms, following former commissioners Park Yong-oh and Koo Bon-neung. Heo's new three-year term is set to begin in January 2027. Heo, a longtime television color commentator, was first elected commissioner in March 2022 to succeed Chung Ji-taik, who stepped down abruptly because of health issues. Heo served the remainder of Chung's term, which ended on Dec. 31, 2023. Heo was unan

results.title: Korean National Symphony Orchestra Academy caps yearlong training with 'Soar' concert
results.content: Young musicians completing a year of intensive orchestral training will take center stage Nov. 28 as the Korean National Symphony Orchestra (KNSO) presents its KNSO Academy concert, "Soar," marking the end of their training and the beginning of their professional musical careers. The concert, scheduled for 5 p.m. at Sejong Arts Center, brings together young musicians who have spent a year developing their performance skills through practical training, mentoring and regular orchestral performances. Since its launch in 2021, the academy has trained 109 musicians, 49 of whom have joined major Korean orchestras, including KBS Symphony Orchestra, Gyeonggi Philharmonic Orchestra and Daejeon Philharmonic Orchestra, representing an employment rate of approximately 45 percent. results.title: Lee, Carney pledge joint efforts to establish stable energy supply chains
results.content: Korean President Lee Jae Myung and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney agreed Thursday to continue their cooperation to build stable and mutually beneficial energy supply chains. The two leaders reached the agreement during a bilateral meeting held on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China. Lee and Carney reviewed energy cooperation between their countries and agreed to continue cooperation to build stable and mutually beneficial energy supply chains, Lee's spokesperson Kim Sung-wan said in a release. The leaders also agreed to jointly seek international cooperation regarding artificial intelligence innovation and safety, Kim said.

results.title: Korean tenants turn to credit cards for paying rent amid rising housing costs
results.content: A 33-year-old office worker in Seoul’s Yongsan District surnamed Lee signed up for an app that lets her pay rent by credit card, after hearing about the service in a news report. Rent takes up a large share of her monthly budget, she said, and having enough cash on hand by the due date can be stressful. “I like that paying by card buys me time until the bill comes due,” Lee said. “I’m still weighing whether that’s worth the fee.” Rent payment apps are gaining ground as housing costs rise, particularly in Seoul, and more landlords switch from "jeonse," or large lump-sum leases, to monthly rentals. The services allow renters who are short on cash to cover their rent if they have enough available credit, but some providers charge fees exceeding 7 percent of the payment amount. results.title: Korea's research rising, but universities must break down silos: WUN chief
results.content: Universities must work more closely with industry, business and government to turn research into real-world impact, and Korean universities are well placed to do so as the country’s research standing rises, according to the head of a global university alliance. Dawn Freshwater, executive director of the Worldwide Universities Network (WUN), made the remarks in an interview with The Korea Times Thursday, during the Times Higher Education Innovation & Impact Summit 2026 at Korea University in Seoul. WUN is a consortium of research-intensive universities across six continents that funds and supports international research collaboration among its members. Freshwater said universities have long been cut off from government, industry and business. results.title: P&G Korea donates 20,000 diapers to support vulnerable families
results.content: P&G Korea, the local unit of U.S. consumer goods giant Procter & Gamble, is donating 20,000 Pampers diapers to families facing financial and social hardships, extending its support for vulnerable children and single-parent households ahead of the year-end holiday season. The donation was made through the Salvation Army Kettle Campaign, with the diapers set to be distributed to Duri Home, a residential facility for single-parent families, other Salvation Army childcare facilities and households raising young children in need. Duri Home provides accommodation and support for single parents raising children younger than 3, helping families establish stable living conditions while preparing for independent lives. results.title: Korean tech giants take different paths in humanoid robot race
results.content: Samsung Electronics and LG Electronics are pursuing markedly different strategies in the robotics market, and the contrast is expected to become more apparent as the two companies showcase their latest technologies and visions at CES 2027. According to industry officials on Thursday, Samsung Electronics is focusing on precise control of robotic hands and arms, as dexterity is considered one of the most critical capabilities for expanding the practical applications of humanoid robots. Unlike conventional robots, whose role was repeating a single rigid motion, humanoid robots are required to perform various work in constantly changing real-world environments. This requires them to go beyond simply grasping and moving objects to handling a wide range of tools and components with precision. results.title: Diageo Korea unveils 2027 Year of the Red Sheep Johnnie Walker Blue Label
results.content: Diageo Korea unveiled a limited-edition Johnnie Walker Blue Label to welcome 2027, pairing its flagship Scotch with bespoke artwork celebrating hope and new beginnings. Released earlier this week, the special bottling is the latest chapter in Johnnie Walker’s annual zodiac collection, a series known for reimagining each year’s animal symbol through distinct artistic collaborations. The limited edition marks the Year of the Red Sheep, also referred to as the Year of the Goat. The latest edition was created in collaboration with Jiayi Li, a Chinese artist based in Paris, whose design draws on the red sheep as a symbol of warmth, dignity and vitality. The packaging connects the animal's gentle appearance and inner determination with Johnnie Walker's longstanding "Keep Walking" philosophy, which emphasizes perseverance and moving toward new possibilities. results.title: Korea becomes world's 4th country to reach $1 tril. in annual exports
results.content: Korea has surpassed $1 trillion in annual exports for the first time in its history, becoming the world's fourth country to reach the milestone after the United States, Germany and China, as a global artificial intelligence (AI) boom drives demand for semiconductors. The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources announced Thursday that the country's cumulative exports reached the $1 trillion mark at 2:09:38 p.m. The achievement comes 19 years after China reached the milestone in 2007, following the U.S. and Germany in 2006. The government projects annual exports will reach approximately $1.17 trillion this year, following last year's record of $709.3 billion. The ministry explained global technology companies’ expanding AI investments were the biggest driver of export growth, boosting demand for semiconductors and computers while pushing up memory chip prices. results.title: Kolmar Group secures Red Bull's Korean distribution rights
results.content: Kolmar Group has secured the Korean distribution rights for Red Bull, the world's No. 1 energy drink brand, as Vice Chairman Yoon Sang-hyun seeks to capitalize on the fast-growing market by adding the Austrian brand to HK inno.N's business portfolio. HK inno.N plans to leverage its nationwide distribution network and experience in building Condition, a popular Korean hangover relief drink, into one of the country's leading brands to expand Red Bull's market share. Launched in Austria in 1987, Red Bull sold approximately 14 billion cans worldwide last year, up 10.2 percent from a year earlier. Its revenue rose 8.6 percent to a record 12.2 billion euros ($14.1 billion). The global energy drink market is also expanding rapidly. results.title: Korea, US, 11 other countries issue statement on cooperation against online scams
results.content: Korea, the United States and 11 other countries released a joint statement Thursday on their cooperation in combating online scams through information sharing, proactive law enforcement and other measures, according to Seoul's foreign ministry. The countries issued a "statement of principles," decrying online scams as "serious and complex" transnational crimes that threaten regional and international peace and security. They included Australia, Canada, Japan, New Zealand, Britain, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. The statement came as Seoul has been striving to address online scams targeting its citizens, following reports of Koreans being abducted and held in Cambodia by criminal rings in recent years. results.title: What Korea can learn from California's 10-flagship university system
results.content: Collaboration, rather than competition, backed by strong leadership and shared governance, has been key to building a University of California (UC) system in which all 10 campuses thrive by developing their own strengths. Darren Cooke, chief innovation and entrepreneurship officer at UC Berkeley, emphasized the importance of strong leadership and a shared governing structure in bringing universities together while allowing each to build on its own strengths. "Every one is amazing, right, and has its own strengths, and I think that's the key. Every one has its own strengths," Cooke said during an interview with The Korea Times. The UC system offers lessons for Korea as the government seeks to strengthen regional flagship national universities and develop them into institutions capable of competing with Seoul National University.
